4th Period.workingNow: Embedding your ROLLER game on your portfolio site and finishing your design document.
4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: One design document in your portfolio repo bringing together your mechanics, dynamics, aesthetic and state map — plus your ROLLER game embedded and playable on your portfolio site — pushed by Sunday night.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can embed my game on my portfolio site so that anyone can play it right next to the design document that explains it.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.16 — Incorporate existing code, media, and libraries into original programs, and give attribution.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.2 — Interacting with others in written English in various communicative forms.
agenda: I do: embed ROLLER on your portfolio site (12 min)
We do: check one portfolio against the rubric (7 min)
You do: embed, then finish your document (23 min)
Exit Ticket: paste your live portfolio link (3 min)
4th Period.connections: Your design document explains a game nobody can play yet. Today you fix that — the base game goes live on your portfolio site, embedded right above the design that says what you are going to do to it. Next week you start building, and every change will show up on that page.

6th Period.workingNow: Typing everything from this week into one game plan the robot can build from.
6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Your completed Game Plan document — two mechanics each with a number, five states, how the mechanics connect to the states, and your first level described — typed and turned in by Sunday night.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can write a complete game plan so that someone who has never seen my game could build it without asking me anything.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.19 — Document programs in order to make them easier to follow, test, and debug.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.10 — Writing literary and informational texts to present, describe, and explain ideas and information.
agenda: Overview: today you write the whole plan (3 min)
I do: what the robot needs to build your game (10 min)
We do: fill in Part 1 together (7 min)
You do: type your game plan (24 min)
Exit Ticket: your game's name and its feeling (3 min)
6th Period.connections: All week you built one piece at a time: two states, then triggers, then a third state, then five. Today every piece goes into one document — your mechanics, your numbers, your states, and what your first level looks like. Next week you hand it to SchoolAI and it builds your game in Game Lab. It can only build what you wrote down.
